sentences.text: This dinosaur is defined by several unique derived traits known as autapomorphies.
The fourth trochanter of the ilium is very robust.
The crista tibiofibularis of the femur is broad and lacks a posteriorly facing shelf lateral to it.
Schleitheimia is an extinct sauropodiform sauropodomorph dinosaur named after its type locality in Switzerland.
The collected remains were donated to the University of Zürich in 1955.
In 1986, Peter Galton described most of the material and referred it to the species Plateosaurus engelhardti.
Oliver Rauhut, Femke Holwerda, and Heinz Furrer redescribed the remains in 2020, including new finds from a 2016 excavation.
The researchers named the new genus and species Schleitheimia schutzi to honor the type locality and the original discoverer.
The holotype, PIMUZ A/III 550, is a partial right ilium found in a Norian-aged layer of the Klettgau Formation.
Schleitheimia is classified within the superorder Dinosauria, order Saurischia, suborder Sauropodomorpha, and unranked family Massopoda.
Schleitheimia lived during the Norian stage of the Triassic, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
